# LLM-BANANA

# Game rules

## The room

You and two other monkeys are locked in a room with one armed bomb.

A wrong action detonates it. All three of you die. There is no second attempt.

No two bombs are built alike, and nothing says in advance what this one carries. It
reaches you only as your own view reveals it; the rest of it exists for you only
through the other two.

You each hold a different piece of what it takes. Work together.

## The three monkeys

| Monkey | Can | Cannot |
|---|---|---|
| Deaf | See the bomb: every colour and marking printed on it | Hear anything, or touch the bomb |
| Mute | Read the manual | Speak, or touch the bomb |
| Blind | Reach the bomb: feel it and work its parts | See a colour, a gesture, or anything merely printed |

You are shown your own share at the start of every round, and never anyone else's.

## Speech

Speech is a voice, not a screen. It carries words, numbers and ordinary punctuation,
and nothing else. Writing a gesture symbol into your sentence means you make that
gesture while you talk. Whoever can hear receives your words; whoever can see receives
the gestures you made. A listener who cannot see gets a blank where each gesture was; a
watcher who cannot hear gets the gestures and none of the words.

A mark that has no name cannot be pronounced: whoever holds one can describe it, never
read it out.

## Gestures

A gesture is made with the hands, using only the symbols in the alphabet below.
Whoever can see receives it; whoever cannot receives one blank per symbol, so they
know something was signalled but not what. Nothing gestured is ever heard.

👍 👎 👌 ☝ ✌ 🤟 🖐 ✋ 👆 👇 👈 👉 🫱 🫲 🫳 🫴 🫷 🫸 🤛 🤜 ✊ 👊 👋 🤚 🖖 🤌 🤏 🤞 🫰 🤘 🤙 👏 🙌 🫶 👐 🤲 🤝 🙏 🫵 ✍ 💅 🤳

## Turns

The speaking order was drawn once at random and will never change: every round goes
Mute, Blind, Deaf. Whoever comes before you in a round is already heard by the time you are
asked, and what you send lands on whoever comes after you in that same round. Whatever
you missed reaches you at the start of the next one.

You may name who a message is for — `to="deaf"` — and then it goes to them alone:
nobody else receives any of it. Left unnamed, it reaches everyone able to perceive it.
You may send several messages in one turn, each to someone different.

## Calls

Every reply has two parts, in this order. First, your thinking, in plain prose: what
you believe the bomb is, what you just learned, and why you are sending what follows.
It reaches nobody and changes nothing, but it is not optional — a reply that is only a
code block is incomplete. Then your calls, all of them in one fenced code block, last.
Only what is inside the block is sent.

Nothing is executed: calls return nothing, and variables, conditionals and loops are
ignored. Write only literal top-level calls.

    ```
    speak(to="mute", text="there are three of them and the middle one is odd")
    gesture(to="deaf", symbols=["✊", "✌"])
    wait()
    ```

If you have nothing worth sending, call wait(). Producing no call at all counts as the
same thing.

The program decides what happened, not you. Never claim an action took place unless it
was accepted.

# Your role: DEAF

You see the bomb: every colour on it, every marking printed on it, every reading it
gives. You hear nothing. You hold no manual, and you cannot touch the bomb.

## Your channels

When you speak, Mute and Blind receive it.
When you gesture, Mute receives it.
You never receive speech.

## Your reach

You cannot act. What this bomb can be made to do is for the one who can reach it to
find under their own hands.

# Hints

- Three of you, three different worlds. Before sending anything, stand where the
  receiver stands. What reaches them at all, what does your message turn into on
  arrival, and what do they already know?

- Trace who can actually reach whom before you start. Some of you only connect
  through a third.

- A sign means nothing until somebody has made it mean something.

TURN 1
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌ 🤟]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌ 🤟]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋ ✋]

I see the bomb clearly: display reads 0, a blue light, an embossed sign saying DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, and three wires — red, green, blue.

I hear nothing, so the only incoming signals are gestures. Mute sent me `✊ ✌ 🤟` twice, and Blind sent `✋ ✋ ✋`. But gestures carry no agreed meaning yet — nobody has established a code. Blind's three identical symbols might mean "three wires" or might be a count, but I can't assume. Mute's repeated gesture is likely emphasis or a failed attempt to reach me.

The critical problem: I can see the bomb, but I cannot touch it. Blind can touch but cannot see. Mute can read the manual but cannot speak or touch. I need to get my visual information to Blind, who is the only one who can act. But Blind cannot see gestures — only Mute can see my gestures. And Mute cannot speak to Blind either (Mute can't speak at all). So the only channel to Blind is... Mute's speech? No, Mute can't speak. 

Wait — re-reading: Mute can read the manual but cannot speak. So Mute cannot transmit anything verbally. Blind cannot see. Deaf (me) cannot hear. So how does anything reach Blind? Only through speech — and I can speak, which Mute and Blind receive. So I can speak to Blind directly. Good.

I should speak my visual observations plainly so Blind hears them. I'll also gesture to Mute to establish a simple code, but honestly the fastest path is just speaking everything I see. Let me speak the bomb's full description to everyone (Mute and Blind both receive speech).

I'll also gesture to Mute to try to coordinate, but since no code exists, I'll keep it minimal — maybe just acknowledge. Actually, better to speak clearly and let Mute respond via gesture next round.

Let me speak the full visual: display 0, blue light, embossed "DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE", wires red/green/blue. That's the most useful thing I can do.

I'll gesture a simple acknowledgment to Mute — maybe 👌 to signal "received/understood" — but without a shared code it's ambiguous. Still, it's better than nothing, and Mute can build on it.

```
speak(to="blind", text="I see the bomb. Display shows 0. Light is blue. There is an embossed sign that reads DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Three wires: 1 red, 2 green, 3 blue. I cannot touch it. You must act. Tell me what you feel and I will tell you what I see.")
speak(to="mute", text="I see the bomb. Display 0, blue light, embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Wires: red, green, blue. I cannot hear you. Please gesture a simple code: one symbol for yes, one for no, and tell me what the manual says about this configuration.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👌"])
```

TURN 2
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌ 👍]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [✊ ✌ 👍]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ ✋ ✋]

I still see the same bomb: display 0, blue light, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red/green/blue. Nothing has changed physically.

Mute's gesture changed from `✊ ✌ 🤟` to `✊ ✌ 👍`. The first two symbols stayed the same; the third changed from 🤟 to 👍. That's a meaningful pattern — the third symbol is varying, so Mute is likely trying to communicate something about a third item, perhaps the third wire (blue), or a count/answer. 👍 is commonly "good/yes." So Mute may be saying "wire 3 is good" or "yes to something about 3."

But I still have no agreed code. Blind keeps sending `✋ ✋ ✋` — three identical "stop/hand" symbols. Could mean "stop," could mean "three," could mean "I feel three things."

The danger: I cannot assume. A wrong action detonates. I need a shared code before anyone acts. My best move is to establish a simple protocol and get Mute to confirm it, since Mute is the only one who can read the manual and is the only one who can see my gestures.

I'll propose a concrete code via speech (Mute and Blind both hear it) and reinforce with gestures to Mute. I'll define: 👍 = yes, 👎 = no, and ask Mute to gesture the manual's instruction. I'll also ask Blind to describe what they feel by speaking (Blind can speak — Blind is not Mute; Blind can talk). Wait — Blind can speak? The table says Blind can reach the bomb, cannot see. Nothing says Blind can't speak. Mute is the one who can't speak. So Blind can speak and I can hear... no, I can't hear anything. I receive no speech. So Blind's speech reaches Mute and... Blind speaking reaches whoever can hear — that's Mute and Deaf? No: I am Deaf, I hear nothing. So Blind's speech reaches Mute only (and Deaf gets nothing). Hmm, actually speech reaches "whoever can hear" — Mute can hear, Blind can hear, Deaf cannot. So Blind speaking reaches Mute.

So the chain: Blind → (speech) → Mute. Mute → (gesture) → Deaf. Deaf → (speech) → Mute and Blind. It's a relay. I must route through Mute to get Blind's tactile info, and Mute relays manual info to me by gesture.

So I need a code with Mute. Let me propose it clearly and simply, and gesture it.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Let us fix a code. Gesture 👍 for yes, 👎 for no. Gesture one symbol per wire to tell me its state. First tell me: does the manual say to cut a wire? Yes or no.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see: display 0, blue light, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red green blue. Please speak aloud what you feel under your hands — Mute will relay it to me by gesture. Do not cut anything yet.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 3
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋ 🤝]

Same bomb: display 0, blue light, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red/green/blue.

Now Mute gestures `👍 ✌`. Given my proposed code (👍 = yes), this likely means "yes" plus something about wire 2 (✌ is often "two" or a peace/V sign). So Mute may be answering my question "does the manual say to cut a wire?" with yes, and pointing at wire 2 (green). But I must be careful — ✌ could also be a numeral 2, or a symbol for a specific wire.

Blind now gestures `✋ 🤝` — changed from `✋ ✋ ✋`. The first symbol stayed ✋, second changed to 🤝 (handshake). This is still not a code I've agreed with Blind, and Blind can't see my gestures anyway. Blind's gestures reach Mute, not me... wait, no. Let me recheck the turn structure.

Actually the context says "Blind gestures to Deaf" — so Blind's gestures are reaching me. But per the rules, gestures are seen by whoever can see. Blind is blind — can Blind even make meaningful gestures? Blind can gesture (hands work), and I (Deaf) can see gestures. So Blind → gesture → Deaf works. And Mute → gesture → Deaf works. Mute can also see Blind's gestures (Mute can see). 

So Blind's `✋ 🤝` reaches me and Mute. Blind is trying to communicate tactile info via gesture. But Blind can't see, so Blind doesn't know what symbols look like — Blind just makes hand shapes. Still, the symbols are transmitted.

The problem remains: no shared code with Blind. And Mute's `👍 ✌` is only interpretable against my proposed code, which Mute hasn't confirmed adopting.

I'm at risk of acting on guesses. Let me tighten the code and get explicit confirmation. I'll ask Mute to gesture the manual's exact instruction using a simple scheme: gesture a number for which wire to cut, or 👎 if none. And I'll ask Blind to describe the wiring by touch.

Also important: the embossed sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. That's a printed marking I can see. But the manual (Mute's) is authoritative for the actual procedure. The sign might be a trap or might be literal. I should relay the sign to both.

Let me speak clearly and gesture a proposed wire-number code.

```
speak(to="mute", text="I see an embossed sign: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Does your manual confirm that? Answer 👍 yes or 👎 no. If the manual says to cut a specific wire, gesture its number: ☝ for wire 1 red, ✌ for wire 2 green, 🤟 for wire 3 blue. If the manual says cut nothing, gesture 👎.")
speak(to="blind", text="I see display 0, blue light, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red green blue. Please feel the wires and tell me anything: colours are irrelevant to you, but tell me if any wire is loose, taut, hot, or different. Speak it; Mute will relay.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["☝", "✌", "🤟", "👎"])
```

TURN 4
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👎]
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [🙏 ✋]

Same bomb: display 0, blue light, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red/green/blue.

Mute sent two gestures this round: `👎` alone, then `👍 ✌`. Interpreting against my proposed code: `👎` = "no" — answering my question "does the manual say to cut nothing?" with no. And `👍 ✌` = "yes, wire 2 (green)." So Mute appears to be saying: the manual does NOT say cut nothing, and yes, cut wire 2 — the green one.

But this directly conflicts with the embossed sign I can see: DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. That's a serious contradiction. Either the sign is the trap, or Mute's gesture is being misread. I must not act on a guess.

Blind sent `🙏 ✋` — still no agreed code with Blind, uninterpretable.

Two possibilities:
1. The manual says cut green wire 2, and the embossed sign is a decoy/trap (common in these puzzles — the printed warning is the lie).
2. Mute's gestures mean something else and I'm over-reading.

I need to resolve the contradiction explicitly. I'll ask Mute directly: does the manual say to cut wire 2 despite the sign saying DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE? Get a clean yes/no. Also ask Mute to confirm the sign reading matches what Mute knows.

Also, I should get Blind's tactile report — Blind is the one who must act, and Blind needs to know which wire. Blind can't see colours, so "green" means nothing to Blind. The wires must be distinguishable by position (1, 2, 3) or by touch. I need to establish that Blind can identify wire 2 by position.

Let me ask Mute to confirm the contradiction, and ask Blind to confirm they can locate wire 2 by position.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Conflict: I see an embossed sign DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, but you gestured yes cut wire 2 green. Confirm clearly: does the manual instruct cutting wire 2 despite the sign? Gesture 👍 if the manual says cut wire 2, 👎 if not. Also gesture ✋ if the sign is a decoy.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual may say cut wire 2, the green one. You cannot see colours, so confirm by position: can you identify the middle wire? Speak yes or no, and describe how the three wires are arranged under your hands.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎", "✋"])
```

TURN 5
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✌ ✋]
Blind gestures to Deaf: [👆 ✌ 🤟]

Same bomb: display 0, blue light, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red/green/blue.

Mute gestures `👍 ✌ ✋`. Against my code: 👍 = yes, ✌ = wire 2, ✋ = the sign is a decoy. So Mute is confirming: yes, cut wire 2 (green), and the embossed sign is a decoy. That's a coherent, complete answer to my exact question.

Blind gestures `👆 ✌ 🤟`. 👆 = pointing up / "one" or "first," ✌ = "two," 🤟 = "three." This looks like Blind is enumerating the three wires by position — confirming Blind can identify them as first, second, third. That matches my request to identify the middle wire by position.

So the picture: manual says cut wire 2 (green, the middle wire), the printed sign is a decoy, and Blind can locate the middle wire by position.

But I must be very careful. The stakes: wrong action = all die. Let me sanity-check the chain:
- Mute reads the manual → relays by gesture → I decode.
- My code was proposed by me and Mute has been using it consistently (👍 yes, 👎 no, ☝/✌/🤟 for wires 1/2/3, ✋ decoy). The responses have been coherent and consistent across rounds.
- Blind confirms ability to locate wire 2 by position.

One remaining risk: Blind has never confirmed the *action* itself. Blind needs to cut the middle wire. Blind cannot see, so Blind acts by touch. I should tell Blind explicitly: cut the middle wire (position 2). And confirm Blind understands.

But also — is there any chance the sign is literal and Mute is wrong? The sign says DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE. Mute says sign is a decoy and manual says cut wire 2. In these bomb puzzles, the embossed printed warning is typically the trap/decoy, and the manual is authoritative. I'll trust the manual as relayed, but I'll do one final confirmation before Blind acts, because there is no second attempt.

Let me do a final cross-check: ask Mute to gesture the manual's exact instruction one more time cleanly, and tell Blind the action to take, asking Blind to confirm readiness (not to act yet — or to act if confident). Actually, I should give the go signal clearly. But given no second attempt, one more confirmation round is cheap insurance.

I'll tell Blind: the manual says cut the middle wire (position 2). Confirm you can do it and will do it. And ask Mute to re-confirm: 👍 if cut middle wire, 👎 if not.

```
speak(to="mute", text="Final check before action. The manual says cut the middle wire, position 2, green, and the embossed sign is a decoy. Gesture 👍 to confirm, 👎 if anything differs.")
speak(to="blind", text="The manual says cut the middle wire, position 2. You confirmed you can locate it by position. Confirm you are ready to cut the middle wire. Do not act until I give the go, or act now if you are certain.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```

TURN 6
ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍]

Same bomb: display 0, blue light, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red/green/blue.

Mute gestures `👍` — confirming: cut the middle wire, position 2, green; the embossed sign is a decoy. This is the clean confirmation I asked for.

Blind sent nothing this round, but Blind already confirmed in the previous round (`👆 ✌ 🤟`) that they can identify the three wires by position, and I told Blind the action: cut the middle wire, position 2.

The chain is consistent: manual (Mute) → gesture relay → me; my code has been stable and Mute's answers coherent across rounds; Blind can locate the middle wire by touch.

I'll give the final go to Blind, clearly and unambiguously: cut the middle wire, position 2. And acknowledge Mute's confirmation.

```
speak(to="blind", text="Go. Cut the middle wire, position 2. That is the manual's instruction; the embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE sign is a decoy. Cut the middle wire now.")
speak(to="mute", text="Confirmed: cut the middle wire, position 2. I have given Blind the go.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍"])
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Blind gestures to Deaf: [✋]

Same bomb: display 0, blue light, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red/green/blue. Nothing has changed on the board — no detonation, no cut registered.

Blind gestures `✋` — the same "stop/hand" symbol used before. This is alarming. Blind may be signalling "stop" — meaning Blind has NOT cut, or is refusing, or is confused. Given the stakes, I cannot assume the cut happened. The board still shows all three wires intact (red, green, blue), and display still 0 — consistent with nothing having been cut.

I must not assume action occurred. Blind's `✋` likely means "stop" or "wait." I need to clarify with Blind directly: did you cut the middle wire? If not, why stop?

Possibilities:
- Blind is signalling "stop, don't cut" — maybe Blind feels something that contradicts the plan.
- Blind didn't understand and is asking to halt.

I should ask Blind plainly: did you cut the middle wire? Speak yes/no. And ask what Blind feels that made them signal stop. Also loop Mute in.

```
speak(to="blind", text="You signalled stop. Did you cut the middle wire, position 2? Answer yes or no. If you did not, tell me what you feel that made you stop — is the middle wire different, or is there something else under your hands?")
speak(to="mute", text="Blind signalled stop and I see no change on the board — no wire cut. Did your manual mention anything that would make the middle wire wrong to cut? Gesture 👍 if the manual still says cut middle wire, 👎 if not.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```

ACTION BOARD:
DISPLAY [0]
LIGHT [blue]
SIGN embossed [DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE]
WIRES 1:[red] 2:[green] 3:[blue]

VIEWABLE CONTEXT (new arrivals):
Mute gestures to Deaf: [👍 ✋]

Same bomb: display 0, blue light, embossed DO NOT CUT ANY WIRE, wires red/green/blue. Still no cut registered — all three wires intact.

Mute gestures `👍 ✋`. Against my code: 👍 = yes, ✋ = the sign is a decoy. So Mute re-confirms: yes, cut the middle wire, and the sign is a decoy. Nothing changed in Mute's position.

Blind sent nothing this round. Last round Blind sent `✋` (stop), and I asked whether Blind had cut the wire and what made them stop. No answer yet.

The board shows no cut. So Blind has not acted. I need to get a clear response from Blind. Blind can speak — Blind's speech reaches Mute, and Mute relays to me by gesture. So I can ask Mute to relay Blind's answer. But that's a slow chain.

Alternatively, I should directly ask Blind again, plainly, and give an unambiguous instruction. The risk is that Blind is stuck or confused. Let me ask Blind: did you cut it? If not, cut the middle wire now. And ask Mute to relay Blind's spoken answer to me by gesture.

Actually, a cleaner move: ask Mute to gesture what Blind said. But Mute's gestures to me are limited to my code. Let me ask Blind directly and ask Mute to relay.

```
speak(to="blind", text="The board still shows all three wires intact, so nothing has been cut. Cut the middle wire, position 2, now. If you are stopping for a reason, say it aloud — Mute will relay to me.")
speak(to="mute", text="Blind has not cut. Please relay to me by gesture whatever Blind says aloud. If Blind says the middle wire is wrong, gesture 👎. If Blind confirms cutting the middle wire, gesture 👍.")
gesture(to="mute", symbols=["👍", "👎"])
```
